<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL" id="Definitions_ClaimHandling" targetNamespace="http://example.org/bpmn/claim-handling">
  <bpmn:process id="Process_ClaimHandling" name="Claim Handling" isExecutable="false">
    <bpmn:laneSet id="LaneSet_ClaimHandling">
      <bpmn:lane id="Lane_ClaimsOfficer" name="Claims Officer">
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>StartEvent_ClaimRegistered</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_ExamineClaim</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_WriteRecommendation</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
      </bpmn:lane>
      <bpmn:lane id="Lane_SeniorClaimsOfficer" name="Senior Claims Officer">
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_CheckRecommendation</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Gateway_ClaimDecision</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>EndEvent_ClaimAccepted</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
      </bpmn:lane>
    </bpmn:laneSet>

    <bpmn:startEvent id="StartEvent_ClaimRegistered" name="Claim registered">
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_RegisteredToExamine</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:startEvent>

    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_ExamineClaim" name="Examine claim">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_RegisteredToExamine</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_ExamineToWrite</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:userTask>

    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_WriteRecommendation" name="Write settlement recommendation">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_ExamineToWrite</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_NotOKToWrite</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_WriteToCheck</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:userTask>

    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_CheckRecommendation" name="Check settlement recommendation">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_WriteToCheck</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_CheckToDecision</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:userTask>

    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_ClaimDecision" name="Claim marked OK?">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_CheckToDecision</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_OKToHandling</bpmn:outgoing>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_NotOKToWrite</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:exclusiveGateway>

    <bpmn:endEvent id="EndEvent_ClaimAccepted" name="Claim handling proceeds">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_OKToHandling</bpmn:incoming>
    </bpmn:endEvent>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_RegisteredToExamine" sourceRef="StartEvent_ClaimRegistered" targetRef="Task_ExamineClaim"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_ExamineToWrite" sourceRef="Task_ExamineClaim" targetRef="Task_WriteRecommendation"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_WriteToCheck" sourceRef="Task_WriteRecommendation" targetRef="Task_CheckRecommendation"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_CheckToDecision" sourceRef="Task_CheckRecommendation" targetRef="Gateway_ClaimDecision"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_OKToHandling" name="OK" sourceRef="Gateway_ClaimDecision" targetRef="EndEvent_ClaimAccepted"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_NotOKToWrite" name="Not OK" sourceRef="Gateway_ClaimDecision" targetRef="Task_WriteRecommendation"/>
  </bpmn:process>
</bpmn:definitions>

rules.instruction: When the description says that one participant checks a work product and that a different participant then marks that product with a verdict (such as OK or Not OK) which decides the next step: Model the check of the work product as its own user task performed by the participant who checks it. Model the verdict as a separate user task performed by the participant who gives it, placed after the check and before the exclusive gateway that routes on the verdict. Label both tasks with the description's own verbs and objects for the check and the verdict. Do not merge the check and the verdict into one task, and do not let the gateway stand in for the verdict task.
rules.situation: the description says that one participant checks a work product and that a different participant then marks that product with a verdict (such as OK or Not OK) which decides the next step

rules.instruction: When the description says a person reviews a prepared item and then marks it with one of two stated outcomes, and the flow continues differently for each outcome: Model the review as a task performed by that person, and model the marking of the outcome as its own task placed directly before the exclusive gateway that tests it. Give each outcome its own outgoing flow labeled with the stated condition. Do not let the review task stand in for the marking task, and do not omit the marking action so that the gateway tests an outcome nobody produced.
rules.situation: the description says a person reviews a prepared item and then marks it with one of two stated outcomes, and the flow continues differently for each outcome

rules.instruction: When the description states an action performed by a role on an item, and a later sentence has an actor give a verdict on that item that decides which branch follows: Model every action the description states as its own task, in the order stated. Keep the review or checking action and the verdict as separate tasks, and do not let one task stand for both. Place the verdict task after the checking task and before the exclusive gateway that routes on the verdict. Also keep any earlier action the description names, such as an examination that precedes the drafting of the output, as its own task rather than dropping it. Branch targets described as continuing or returning to an earlier activity should be modeled as tasks or flows that carry the described action, not as an end event that drops it.
rules.situation: the description states an action performed by a role on an item, and a later sentence has an actor give a verdict on that item that decides which branch follows

rules.instruction: When the description states that a verdict branch returns the item to an earlier activity, while the activity that precedes that earlier activity in the forward flow also leads into it, so the earlier activity is entered from two flows: Place an exclusive merge gateway immediately before the earlier activity. Route both the forward flow from the preceding step and the returning flow from the verdict branch into this merge gateway, and let the merge gateway's single outgoing flow lead to the earlier activity. Do not connect the returning flow or the forward flow directly to the activity, and do not join the two flows with a parallel gateway.
rules.situation: the description states that a verdict branch returns the item to an earlier activity, while the activity that precedes that earlier activity in the forward flow also leads into it, so the earlier activity is entered from two flows
